prompt: Write a short report title as a single line based on the supplied findings. Return only the title as plain text.

findings.main_response: The neuron primarily detects a Colorado named-entity/jurisdiction frame in the causal prefix, firing strongly on explicit Colorado or Colorado-derived names and on Colorado-linked institutions, places, statutory citations, contact/URL/local-media strings, state-history facts, and university/science contexts. Strong activation requires that Colorado-specific cue to precede the scored token, with the peak often on an adjacent space, function word, digit, or punctuation inside the name/citation/contact frame; continuation after the anchor does not count. Matched controls bound this: a generic country slot in the Colorado-name template was near zero, a bare grant number in the statutory-reference template and generic URL/phone forms were weak, and explicit Colorado in the prefix was usually positive but not sufficient, so the response is frame-specific rather than format- or place-name-alone.
findings.negative_pole: Strong negative activation is reliably produced only by formal other-jurisdiction administrative, contact, or citation strings in the causal prefix, such as North Dakota Game and Fish CWD contact with phone (701) 328-1504 (−39.25), N.D.C.C. § 28-33-02 (−28), a Qinghai grant/area block (−46.75), and a full New Mexico administrative block (−27.25). This is narrower than non-Colorado place naming: Bolivia (+157), Nepal (+28), Texas (−1.203), Bismarck, North Dakota (−3.25), and an ordinary Montana 406 contact (+6.66) are positive or weak, while generic phone, URL, citation punctuation, digits, or Pub. L. No. 90-284 (+0.42) are weak or not reliable by format alone. The corpus negative tail is sparse with many no-visible-cue labels, and presence of Colorado in the prefix does not prevent local suppression at a competing other-jurisdiction anchor, so the evidence supports only the formal other-jurisdiction administrative/legal frame, not a broad other-place or format-only negative rule.
findings.what_would_change_my_mind: A future controlled sweep should vary whether non-Colorado place names appear bare or inside formal administrative/contact/citation strings while holding the template, punctuation/digits, scored token position, causal-prefix length, and same-position controls fixed; if bare-name versions become consistently strongly negative, comparable to the North Dakota administrative block, and the formal-frame versions add no further negativity, the rival broad non-Colorado place-name rule would be favored and the current administrative-frame specificity narrowed. Because the existing Bolivia and Nepal cases are strongly positive and the Texas control is only weakly negative, this would be a new result rather than confirmation of the present explanation, and activation/product plus ablation KL against controls would be the measured outcomes.

output.text: L55_N11703: Colorado Jurisdiction-Frame Detector with Formal Other-Jurisdiction Administrative Suppression
